items.title: AI virtual assistant for business requests
items.challenge: Make it easier to receive product orders, appointments, and service requests without forcing customers through rigid processes or lengthy forms.
constraints: Customers may write freely and omit required information.
Requests can arrive through different communication channels.
The business needs clear information before fulfilling the order, appointment, or service.
items.role: I designed and developed the virtual assistant, the web experience, and the workflow that transforms a conversation into a request the business owner can understand.
decisions: Use conversational AI to collect missing information through natural questions.
Orchestrate automations with n8n and store structured information in Supabase.
Integrate ElevenLabs to extend the assistant experience to voice interactions.
Keep final approval and execution in the hands of the responsible user.
Deploy the web experience on Vercel and its supporting services on Render.
implementation: Integrated AI models such as ChatGPT to interpret conversations.
Persisted customers, requests, and operational statuses with Supabase.
Automated workflows with n8n and integrated voice capabilities through ElevenLabs.
Created workflows for orders, appointments, and service requests.
Structured the collected data so the business can review each request.
Deployed the assistant website and its services using Vercel and Render.
results: A conversational experience capable of guiding customers and collecting the required details.
Organized requests that the responsible user can review and fulfill.
A reusable foundation for different businesses and customer service channels.
items.lessons: AI works best as an assistant when it reduces customer friction, structures information, and keeps the final decision in human hands.

items.title: Private NAS cloud with Raspberry Pi
items.challenge: Build a low-cost private cloud for storing and accessing files from anywhere without relying on a traditional cloud provider.
constraints: Use of a Raspberry Pi and multiple drives connected through a hub.
Remote access without directly exposing storage to the Internet.
Need to separate folders and permissions for different users.
items.role: I designed the solution and configured storage, remote access, users, and permissions for shared folders.
decisions: Use Tailscale to establish private remote access between devices.
Centralize external drives in a NAS managed by the Raspberry Pi.
Define users and permissions according to the folders each person can read or modify.
implementation: Configured a Raspberry Pi as a NAS server.
Mounted and managed drives connected through a hub.
Configured shared folder services, users, and permissions.
Integrated Tailscale to access the private cloud from any location.
results: A functional private cloud available remotely through a secure connection.
Centralized storage using personally owned hardware.
Access control by user and folder.
items.lessons: A home-built solution can provide control and privacy, but remote access, permissions, availability, and drive protection must be carefully designed.

items.title: Cross-platform business application with Flutter
items.status: Developed, not released to app stores
items.challenge: Build a cross-platform business application for managing products and users, with authentication and cloud persistence.
constraints: The same codebase had to support Android and iOS.
The application needed a clear separation between UI, business logic, and data access.
Development was completed, but publishing to Google Play and the App Store was outside the project scope.
items.role: I designed and developed the full application, defined its architecture, and integrated Firebase services and Google Sign-In.
decisions: Use Flutter to share most of the code across platforms.
Apply Clean Architecture to decouple presentation, domain, and data layers.
Use Firebase for authentication, user management, and data persistence.
implementation: Developed modules for product and user management.
Integrated Firebase database and services.
Implemented authentication and Google Sign-In.
Organized the project into layers using Flutter ecosystem dependencies.
results: A functional application developed for Android and iOS environments.
Source code retained and organized according to Clean Architecture.
Centralized product, user, and authentication management through Firebase.
items.lessons: Completing a functional application and publishing it are separate stages; its architecture and code were developed, while distribution, signing, and store review remained outside the scope.

items.title: Angular modernization and microfrontend architecture
items.challenge: Modernize Angular applications integrated into a microfrontend architecture without stopping the platform's functional growth.
constraints: Existing projects with different versions and dependencies.
Required integration with a root application and other microfrontends.
Need to continue delivering features and resolving incidents during modernization.
items.role: I contributed to the migrations, resolved incompatibilities, upgraded dependencies, and created new microfrontends from their initial configuration.
decisions: Align each project with compatible Angular and dependency versions.
Keep a consistent Single-SPA configuration to simplify integration.
Validate application behavior after every upgrade.
implementation: Migrated applications from Angular 11 to Angular 18.
Subsequently upgraded Angular 18 applications to Angular 21.
Created projects from the ground up and configured Single-SPA.
Resolved compatibility issues and complex frontend defects.
results: Applications upgraded and prepared to keep evolving on modern Angular versions.
New microfrontends consistently integrated with the main application.
Improved stability and user experience through continuous incident resolution.
items.lessons: A migration does not end when the application compiles: it must preserve integration, functional behavior, and the team's ability to continue delivering value.

items.title: Reliable PDF document management
items.challenge: Build an application from the ground up to store, search, and download virtualized documents while preventing file corruption and inefficient retrieval.
constraints: Documents had to preserve their integrity during storage and download.
Searches had to remain efficient as the volume of information grew.
The solution had to cover the full lifecycle, from analysis to IIS deployment.
items.role: I designed and developed the application, worked on its persistence model, optimized queries and indexes, and supported its deployment and continuous improvement in production.
decisions: Separate document metadata from its storage mechanism.
Strengthen validations across upload and download workflows.
Review relationships, queries, and indexes based on actual search patterns.
implementation: Developed the application with ASP.NET, C#, and JavaScript.
Implemented workflows to store, locate, and download PDF files.
Resolved issues that caused document corruption.
Optimized indexes and queries in relational databases.
results: More reliable document management during storage and retrieval.
More efficient searches and downloads through relationship and index improvements.
Institutional processes centralized in a custom-built application.
items.lessons: In a document solution, file integrity and data design must be solved as one problem rather than as isolated layers.

items.title: Reverse engineering and improvement of legacy databases
items.challenge: Identify the root cause of issues in financial and administrative systems whose behavior depended on logic distributed across applications and legacy databases.
constraints: Incomplete technical knowledge about some existing processes.
Complex stored procedures and logic implemented through triggers.
Coexistence of ASP.NET Framework and PowerBuilder applications.
items.role: I analyzed data flows, performed reverse engineering, resolved defects, and implemented new features across applications and database objects.
decisions: Trace each process from the user interface to the queries and objects executed in SQL Server.
Audit stored procedures before changing their behavior.
Preserve compatibility with existing applications while improving the underlying logic.
implementation: Analyzed tables, relationships, and dependencies between objects.
Created and modified stored procedures and triggers.
Developed queries and CRUD operations.
Audited and optimized complex stored procedures.
results: Identified and resolved issues that were difficult to locate from the application layer.
Added new features without breaking compatibility with legacy systems.
Produced clearer and more maintainable database processes after analysis.
items.lessons: Effective reverse engineering requires understanding the business process first; optimizing a query without knowing its purpose can move the problem elsewhere in the system.

items.title: Frontend security and more reliable delivery
items.challenge: Reduce security risks in a banking application without affecting user experience or stopping the delivery of new features.
constraints: Sensitive information handled through the frontend.
Need to mitigate vulnerabilities in an application under continuous development.
Release processes and pipelines connected to multiple projects.
items.role: I mitigated vulnerabilities, strengthened password and encryption workflows, resolved complex incidents, and contributed to release and pipeline improvements.
decisions: Apply validation rules that prevent weak or easily compromised passwords.
Protect sensitive information through end-to-end encryption.
Include security corrections in the regular delivery workflow.
implementation: Strengthened password handling and validation.
Added encryption to sensitive information exchanges.
Resolved vulnerabilities and complex frontend defects.
Improved tasks related to releases and pipelines.
results: Greater protection for information processed by the application.
Password workflows made more resistant to weak credentials.
More reliable delivery with continuous functional improvements.
items.lessons: Frontend security delivers more value when it is part of design and delivery rather than treated as an isolated correction at the end.

columnOne.note: On the frontend side, I have mitigated security vulnerabilities in the application by implementing measures such as input validation, using Content Security Policy (CSP), and protecting against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. columnOne.title: Lazy loading
columnOne.note: I was implement lazy loading on forntend, this is a technique that allows you to load modules or components only when they are needed, rather than loading everything at once when the application starts. This can significantly improve the performance of your application, especially if it has a large number of routes and components. By using lazy loading, you can reduce the initial load time and improve the user experience by loading only the necessary resources when they are required. 🛠️
